title: Κάστωρ
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 153 (= Perry 118). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Κάστωρ ἐστὶ ζῷον τετράπουν ἐν λίμνῃ νεμόμενον.
sentences.tr: Kastōr esti zōion tetrapoun en limnēi nemomenon.
sentences.l: The beaver is a four-footed animal that feeds in a marsh.
sentences.n: κάστωρ is the beaver; the Greek word is also the man's name Castor. λίμνη is standing water — a pool or marsh, not a running river. νεμόμενον is the middle of νέμω, used of animals grazing or feeding at pasture.

sentences.t: Τούτου λέγεται τὰ αἰδοῖα εἴς τινας θεραπείας χρήσιμα εἶναι.
sentences.tr: Toutou legetai ta aidoia eis tinas therapeias chrēsima einai.
sentences.l: Of this animal the genitals are said to be useful for certain cures.
sentences.n: A neuter plural subject, τὰ αἰδοῖα, takes a singular verb, λέγεται — regular Greek, and worth expecting from here on. The drug castoreum, named after the animal, was a standing item in ancient pharmacy, and ancient writers took it to come from the beaver's testicles.

sentences.t: Καὶ δή, εἴ ποτέ τις αὐτὸν θεασάμενος διώκει ἐκτέμνειν βουλόμενος, εἰδὼς οὗ χάριν διώκεται, μέχρι μέν τινος φεύγει τῇ τῶν ποδῶν ταχύτητι συγχρώμενος, πρὸς τὸ ὁλόκληρον ἑαυτὸν διαφυλάξαι· ἐπειδὰν δὲ περικατάληπτος γένηται, ἀποκόπτων τὰ ἑαυτοῦ αἰδοῖα ῥίπτει καὶ οὕτως τῆς σωτηρίας τυγχάνει.
sentences.tr: Kai dē, ei pote tis auton theasamenos diōkei ektemnein boulomenos, eidōs hou charin diōketai, mechri men tinos pheugei tēi tōn podōn tachytēti synchrōmenos, pros to holoklēron heauton diaphylaxai· epeidan de perikatalēptos genētai, apokoptōn ta heautou aidoia rhiptei kai houtōs tēs sōtērias tynchanei.
sentences.l: And indeed, if ever someone, having caught sight of him, pursues him, wishing to cut them out, he — knowing on what account he is being pursued — flees up to a point, making use of the swiftness of his feet, so as to keep himself entire; but when he is hemmed in on every side, cutting off his own genitals he throws them away, and so obtains his deliverance.
sentences.i: And so, if ever a man sights him and gives chase meaning to cut them out, the beaver, knowing what he is hunted for, runs for a while on the speed of his feet, to save himself whole; but once he is caught all round, he cuts off his own genitals, throws them away, and so wins his life.
sentences.n: εἰδώς is nominative and stands next to τις, but it belongs to the unexpressed subject of φεύγει — the beaver, who is the one being pursued. οὗ χάριν, the genitive relative with χάριν, is simply "for what reason". μέχρι μέν τινος, "up to a certain point", is answered by ἐπειδὰν δέ, "but once…". συγχράομαι takes the dative of what one uses. πρὸς τό with the infinitive states purpose, and ὁλόκληρον agrees with ἑαυτόν: to keep himself entire. περικατάληπτος is a rare compound, "caught all round"; it marks the moment escape ends.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων φρόνιμοί εἰσιν ὅσοι διὰ χρήματα ἐπιβουλευόμενοι ἐκεῖνα ὑπερορῶσιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ τῇ σωτηρίᾳ μὴ κινδυνεύειν.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn anthrōpōn phronimoi eisin hosoi dia chrēmata epibouleuomenoi ekeina hyperorōsin hyper tou tēi sōtēriāi mē kindyneuein.
sentences.l: So too, among men, those are prudent who, being plotted against because of money, disregard those things so as not to put their safety in danger.
sentences.i: So too, among men, the prudent are those who, when they are plotted against for their money, let the money go rather than hazard their lives.
sentences.n: τῶν ἀνθρώπων is a partitive genitive picked up by ὅσοι, "all those who". ὑπὲρ τοῦ with the articular infinitive states purpose. κινδυνεύω takes the dative of what is put at risk; σωτηρία here is a man's safety, his life itself.
